mnemonics: pot(有力的) + ent + ate(人) → 有力量的人 → 统治者

definitions.english: likely to develop into a particular type of person or thing in the future

examples.sentence: The company has identified 60 potential customers.

mnemonics: pot(有力的) + ent + ial → 潜在的， 可能的

definitions.english: to cause to be potent

examples.sentence: Circulating exosomes potentiate tumor malignant properties in a mouse model of chronic sleep fragmentation.

mnemonics: potent(强有力的) + -iate(动词后缀) → 使变得强有力 → 加强

definitions.english: to make or be troubled or upset
a commotion, fuss, or disturbance

examples.sentence: Don't get into a pother over such a minor mistake.

mnemonics: pother(听起来像 bother) → 烦扰，骚动

definitions.english: a medicinal or magical or poisonous beverage

examples.sentence: The witch brewed a mysterious potion in her cauldron.

mnemonics: pot(喝) + -ion(名词后缀) → 可饮用的液体 → 药水

definitions.english: A potpourri of things is a collection of various items that were not originally intended to form a group

examples.sentence: ...a potpourri of architectural styles from all over the world.

mnemonics: pot(锅) + pour(倾倒)+ri → 倒在一个锅里 → 混杂物

definitions.english: To take a potshot at someone or something means to shoot at them without taking the time to aim carefully

examples.sentence: The critic took a few potshots at the director's latest film.

mnemonics: pot(锅) + shot(射击) → 原指为了填饱肚子向锅里射击猎物(不讲究瞄准) → 盲目射击/肆意抨击

definitions.english: growing indoors in a pot

examples.sentence: a potted plant

mnemonics: pot(花盆/罐子) + -ed(形容词后缀) → 放在盆/罐里的

definitions.english: objects made out of baked clay
definitions.chinese: 制陶； 制陶工艺； 陶器

examples.sentence: Native American pottery

mnemonics: pot(罐子) + ery(名词后缀，表示工艺/场所) → 制作罐子的工艺/陶器

definitions.chinese: 使成袋状； 将装入袋内

definitions.english: a small leather, cloth, or plastic bag that you can keep things in, and which is sometimes attached to a belt

examples.sentence: a money pouch

mnemonics: pouch(发音似“泡”+“吃”) → 像个鼓鼓的泡，可以装吃的袋子

definitions.english: a medical dressing consisting of a soft heated mass of meal or clay that is spread on a cloth and applied to the skin to treat inflamed areas or improve circulation etc.

examples.sentence: She applied a warm herbal poultice to her swollen ankle.

mnemonics: 源自拉丁语 puls (粥/糊状物) → 像粥一样敷在患处的药

definitions.english: flesh of chickens or turkeys or ducks or geese raised for food

examples.sentence: The farm specializes in raising organic poultry for local markets.

mnemonics: poul(小鸡/小动物，源自pullus) + try(后缀) → 饲养的家禽

definitions.english: to suddenly move forward and attack someone or something, after waiting to attack them
the act of pouncing; a spring or swoop

examples.sentence: The cat was hiding in the bushes, ready to pounce.

mnemonics: pounce与ounce(盎司/少量)谐音，联想：像猫一样轻盈地扑向猎物，动作虽快但像盎司一样轻。

definitions.english: to hit something very hard several times and make a lot of noise, damage it, break it into smaller pieces etc

examples.sentence: He began pounding the keyboard of his computer.

mnemonics: pound(重击) 谐音“胖的” → 胖子走路重重地踩地 → 猛击/重击

definitions.english: a disdainful grimace
definitions.chinese: (尤指撅嘴或板着脸)表示不悦

examples.sentence: She pouted when I told her she couldn't go to the party.

mnemonics: pout(发音类似“泡”的嘴型) → 嘴唇向前突出 → 撅嘴

definitions.english: the state of having little or no money and few or no material possessions

examples.sentence: Millions of people in the region are living in abject poverty.

mnemonics: pover(poor贫穷) + ty(名词后缀) → 贫穷状态

definitions.english: a solid substance in the form of tiny loose particles; a solid that has been pulverized

examples.sentence: She applied a light dusting of powder to her face.
The dry snow was like fine powder under our skis.

mnemonics: 源自古法语 poudre (灰尘) → 细小的粉末

definitions.english: possession of controlling influence

examples.sentence: The president has the power to veto legislation.
Solar panels power the entire building.

mnemonics: 源自古法语 poeir (能够) → 拥有做某事的能力

definitions.english: lacking power

examples.sentence: The government felt powerless to stop the spread of the economic crisis.

mnemonics: power(力量) + less(无) → 没有力量的

definitions.english: s usable for a specific purpose
definitions.chinese: 能实行的， 可行的， 适用的

examples.sentence: The committee proposed a practicable solution to reduce carbon emissions.

mnemonics: practic(做/实践) + able(能……的) → 能做到的 → 可行的

definitions.english: concerned with actual use or practice
definitions.chinese: 实用的； 实际的； 现实的

examples.sentence: The course provides students with practical experience in the field.

mnemonics: pract(做/行动) + -ical(形容词后缀) → 能够付诸行动的 → 实用的

definitions.english: someone who practices a learned profession

examples.sentence: The clinic is staffed by experienced medical practitioners.

mnemonics: pract(实践) + -ition(名词后缀) + -er(人) → 实践某职业的人

definitions.english: dealing with problems in a sensible practical way instead of strictly following a set of ideas

examples.sentence: Williams took a more pragmatic approach to management problems.
Rather than make a philosophical appeal to the Congressmen, the Speaker decided to take a far more pragmatic approach, making small side-deals that would add votes to his bill.

mnemonics: prag(做) + matic → 付诸行动的 → 务实的， 注重实效的

definitions.english: a treeless grassy plain

examples.sentence: The bison roamed freely across the vast prairie.

mnemonics: 源自法语 prairie (草地)，词根 pr- (草地/草场) + -airie (场所) → 大草原

definitions.english: to walk or dance with high steps or large movements, especially in a confident way

examples.sentence: The children pranced around the room in their new costumes.

mnemonics: 那个法国(France)人昂首阔步(prance)地走在大街上

definitions.english: a trick, especially one which is played on someone to make them look silly

examples.sentence: a childish prank

mnemonics: 注意不要和plank(n. 厚木板)相混

definitions.english: someone who plays practical jokes on others
definitions.chinese: 顽皮的人， 爱开玩笑的人

examples.sentence: The class prankster replaced the teacher's chalk with a piece of white cheese.

mnemonics: prank(恶作剧) + ster(人) → 搞恶作剧的人

definitions.english: to talk in a meaningless boring way about something

examples.sentence: They sat in the cafe and continued to prate about their neighbors for hours.

mnemonics: 和prattle(v. 闲聊)一起记

definitions.english: n idle or foolish and irrelevant talk
definitions.chinese: 说孩子气的话； 闲聊

examples.sentence: She began to prattle on about her garden, ignoring the serious tone of the meeting.

mnemonics: prat(傻瓜) + tle(小动作) → 像傻瓜一样喋喋不休

definitions.english: any of various edible decapod crustaceans

examples.sentence: We ordered a platter of grilled jumbo prawns for the main course.

mnemonics: prawn(发音类似“胖”) → 这种虾长得比较胖 → 对虾

definitions.english: to talk about a religious subject in a public place, especially in a church during a service

examples.sentence: He traveled the southern states, preaching the gospel .

mnemonics: p(看作priest， 牧师) + reach(到达) → 牧师到达 → 布道， 讲道

definitions.english: inclined to or marked by tedious moralization

examples.sentence: He gave a preachy speech about the dangers of social media that bored the entire audience.

mnemonics: preach(布道/说教) + y(形容词后缀) → 爱说教的

definitions.english: a statement at the beginning of a book, document, or talk, explaining what it is about
definitions.chinese: 前言， 序言； 先兆

examples.sentence: Harding gave him the news without preamble (= without saying anything else before it ) .

mnemonics: pre(在…之前) + amble(缓行， 漫步) → 走在前面 → 前言

definitions.english: a precarious situation or state is one which may very easily or quickly become worse

examples.sentence: Her health remained precarious, despite the treatment.
the company’s precarious financial position
People smoke to relax and forget their cares, but ironically, in terms of health risks, smoking is far more precarious than either mountain-climbing or skydiving.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + car(汽车) + ious → 在汽车前面 → 危险的

definitions.english: a precautionary measure warding off impending danger or damage or injury etc.

examples.sentence: They took every possible precaution to ensure the safety of the passengers.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + caut(小心/警惕) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先小心 → 预防措施

definitions.english: taken in advance to protect against possible danger or failure

examples.sentence: The government took precautionary measures to prevent the spread of the virus.

mnemonics: pre(提前) + caution(小心/警告) + ary(形容词后缀) → 提前小心以防万一的

definitions.english: to happen or exist before something or someone, or to come before something else in a series

examples.sentence: a type of cloud that precedes rain
Lunch will be preceded by a short speech from the chairman.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + ced(走) + e → 走在…之前 → 早于

definitions.english: status established in order of importance or urgency

examples.sentence: Safety must take precedence over speed in this project.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + ced(走) + ence(名词后缀) → 走在前面 → 优先

definitions.english: an action or official decision that can be used to give support to later actions or decisions

examples.sentence: The Obama administration and police officers around the country say no, and their precedent is the past.
There is no historical precedent that can tell us what happens to established democracies when most citizens go years, even decades, without an improvement in their standard of living.
An east London school has set a precedent by fining pupils who break the rules.

The principal explained that even though one student had done modelling work outside of school, the outfits that student wore in those photographs in no way established a precedent for what could be worn at school dances.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + ced(走) + ent(名词后缀) → 走在前面的事 → 先例

definitions.english: existing or coming before

examples.sentence: The preceding chapter explains the basic concepts of the theory.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + ced(走) + ing → 走在前面的 → 先前的

definitions.english: A precept is a general rule that helps you to decide how you should behave in particular circumstances
definitions.chinese: 箴言， 格言； 规则

examples.sentence: ...an electoral process based on the central precept that all people are born equal.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + cept(拿住) → 预先接受的话 → 格言

definitions.english: the motion of a spinning body (as a top) in which it wobbles so that the axis of rotation sweeps out a cone

examples.sentence: The precession of the Earth's axis causes the position of the stars to shift very slowly over thousands of years.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + cess(行走) + ion(名词后缀) → 先行运动 → 进动

definitions.english: a district of a city or town marked out for administrative purposes

examples.sentence: The police precinct covers the entire downtown area.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + cinct(捆绑/限制) → 预先划定界限的区域 → 管辖区

definitions.english: of high worth or cost

examples.sentence: She keeps all her precious memories in an old wooden box.
His precious attitude toward art made him unpopular with his peers.

mnemonics: pre(预先/在前) + ci(看作) + ous(形容词后缀) → 预先看重的东西 → 珍贵的

definitions.english: a very steep cliff

examples.sentence: The country is standing on the precipice of a major economic crisis.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + cip(头) + ice → 头朝前掉下去的地方 → 悬崖

definitions.english: an agent that causes a precipitate to form

examples.sentence: The company's precipitant decision to cut staff led to a massive strike.

mnemonics: pre(提前) + cipit(头) + ant → 提前把头探出去 → 鲁莽的/下落的

definitions.english: to make something serious happen suddenly or more quickly than was expected
definitions.chinese: 使突然降临， 加速， 促成

definitions.english: happening or done too quickly, and not thought about carefully

examples.sentence: The riot was precipitated when four black men were arrested.

Instead of conducting a thorough investigation after the city hall break-in, the governor acted precipitately, accusing his staff of aiding and abetting the criminals.
The government's mishandling the hurricane's aftermath precipitated a widespread outbreak of looting and other criminal activity.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + cip(落下) + it + ate → 预先落下 → 使突然降临， 加速

definitions.english: the quantity of water falling to earth at a specific place within a specified period of time

examples.sentence: The region has seen record levels of precipitation this year.
His precipitation in making the decision led to a costly mistake.

mnemonics: pre(提前) + cipit(头) + ation(名词后缀) → 头先着地 → 仓促/坠落 → 降水/沉淀

definitions.english: dangerously high or steep

examples.sentence: a precipitous path
He was expecting a precipitous rise in the value of a "hot" tech stock, so he was disappointed when it only inched up a dollar or two each day.

mnemonics: precipit(落下/头朝下) + ous(形容词后缀) → 像从高处落下般陡峭的/急促的

definitions.english: make a summary (of)

examples.sentence: The student wrote a brief précis of the lengthy historical document.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + cis(切，如decide/concise) → 预先切好的精华 → 摘要

definitions.english: precise information, details etc are exact, clear, and correct
definitions.chinese: 精确的， 准确的， 确切的

examples.sentence: precise sales figures
It was difficult to get precise information.
‘She’s a lot older than you, isn’t she?’ ‘Fifteen years, to be precise .’

mnemonics: pre(表加强) + cis(切) + e → 细心地切下 → 精确的

definitions.english: n the quality of being reproducible in amount or performance

examples.sentence: The surgeon performed the operation with remarkable precision.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + cis(切) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先切好 → 精确的

definitions.english: If something precludes an event or action, it prevents the event or action from happening

examples.sentence: At 84, John feels his age precludes too much travel.
The manager specified that all other gates be locked, to preclude the possibility of persons without tickets entering the arena undetected.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + clud(关闭) + e → 预先关闭 → 预防， 排除

definitions.english: a precocious child shows intelligence or skill at a very young age, or behaves in an adult way – sometimes used to show disapproval in British English

examples.sentence: a precocious child who walked and talked early
Though only seven years old, she was a precocious chess prodigy, able to beat players twice her age.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + coc(煮) + ious → 提前煮好的 → 早熟的

definitions.english: conceive beforehand

examples.sentence: It is difficult to judge a new culture without being influenced by what we have already preconceived.

mnemonics: pre(提前) + conceive(构思/设想) → 提前构思 → 预想

definitions.english: a belief or opinion that you have already formed before you know the actual facts, and that may be wrong

examples.sentence: Did you have any preconceptions about the sort of people who did computing?

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + conception(观念) → 先入之见

definitions.english: something that happened or existed before something else and influenced its development

examples.sentence: He said that the deal should not be seen as a precursor to a merger.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + curs(跑) + or → 跑在前面的人 → 先驱

definitions.english: be earlier in time; go back further

examples.sentence: These cave paintings predate the invention of writing by thousands of years.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + date(日期) → 日期在前 → 早于

definitions.english: the act of preying by a predator who kills and eats the prey

examples.sentence: The study examines how predation affects the population dynamics of small rodents.

mnemonics: pre(预先/在前) + dat(给予/拿取) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先盯上并夺取 → 捕食

definitions.english: an animal that kills and eats other animals

examples.sentence: With no natural predators on the island, the herd increased rapidly.

mnemonics: pred(掠夺) + at + or → 食肉动物

definitions.english: a predatory animal kills and eats other animals for food

examples.sentence: predatory pricing

mnemonics: pre(预先/向前) + dat(给予/拿取) + ory → 预先拿走别人的 → 掠夺的

definitions.english: someone who had your job before you started doing it

examples.sentence: Kennedy’s predecessor as President was the war hero Dwight Eisenhower.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + de + cess(走) + or → 在前面走的人 → 前任， 前辈

definitions.english: to foreordain; determine beforehand

examples.sentence: Some people believe that their success was predestined by fate.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + destine(注定) → 预先注定

definitions.english: to determine beforehand
definitions.chinese: 预先注定； 预先决定

examples.sentence: Our genetic makeup does not necessarily predetermine our future success.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + determine(决定) → 预先决定

definitions.english: a situation from which extrication is difficult especially an unpleasant or trying one

examples.sentence: The company is in a difficult predicament after losing its biggest client.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dic(说/断言) + ament → 预先被断言(陷入麻烦) → 困境

definitions.english: make a prediction about; tell in advance

examples.sentence: Experts predict that the global economy will recover by next year.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dict(说) → 预先说出来 → 预测

definitions.english: if something or someone is predictable, you know what will happen or what they will do – sometimes used to show disapproval

examples.sentence: The snow had a predictable effect on traffic.
an entertaining but predictable film
Logan’s reaction was predictable.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dict(说) + able(能…的) → 能预先说出来的 → 可预知的

definitions.english: the act of predicting (as by reasoning about the future)

examples.sentence: The meteorologist's prediction of heavy rain proved to be accurate.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dict(说) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先说出来 → 预测

definitions.english: if you have a predilection for something, especially something unusual, you like it very much

examples.sentence: ...his predilection for fast cars and fast horses.
Monte had a predilection for the fine things in life: Cuban cigars, 200 dollar bottles of wine, and trips to the French Riviera.

mnemonics: pre + dilection(看作direction， 趋向) → 兴趣的趋向 → 偏爱， 嗜好

definitions.english: to make someone more likely to suffer from a particular health problem
definitions.chinese: 使预先有倾向； 易受感染

examples.sentence: They take pains to hire people whose personalities predispose them to serve customers well.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dispose(安排/处理) → 预先安排好倾向 → 使易受影响

definitions.english: an inclination beforehand to interpret statements in a particular way

examples.sentence: Regular exercise can reduce your genetic predisposition to heart disease.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + dis(分开) + posit(放置) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先放置好的倾向

definitions.english: more powerful, more common, or more easily noticed than others
definitions.chinese: 支配的， 占优势的， 主导的

examples.sentence: the predominant group in society
In this painting, the predominant colour is black.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + dominant(统治的) → 在前面统治的 → 支配的， 占优势的

definitions.english: much greater in number or influence

examples.sentence: The audience was predominantly female.

mnemonics: pre(预先/在前) + domin(统治/控制) + ant(形容词后缀) + ly(副词后缀) → 预先控制局面的 → 占优势地

definitions.english: If one type of person or thing predominates in a group, there is more of that type of person or thing in the group than of any other
definitions.chinese: 统治； 占优势， 以…为主

examples.sentence: In older age groups women predominate because men tend to die younger.

mnemonics: pre(预先/在前) + domin(统治/控制) + ate(动词后缀) → 预先占据统治地位 → 占优势

definitions.english: n high status importance owing to marked superiority

examples.sentence: The university is known for its preeminence in the field of quantum physics.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + emin(突出) + ence(名词后缀) → 突出于众人之前 → 卓越

definitions.english: If someone or something is preeminent in a group, they are more important, powerful, or capable than other people or things in the group
definitions.chinese: 出类拔萃的， 杰出的

examples.sentence: ...some of the preeminent names in baseball.

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + eminent(著名的) → 比著名的人还著名 → 出类拔萃的

definitions.english: acquire for oneself before others can do so

examples.sentence: A governmental warning about an imminent terrorist attack would preempt ordinary network programming on television.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + empt(拿到) → 预先拿到 → 以优先权取得

definitions.english: the judicial principle asserting the supremacy of federal over state legislation on the same subject
definitions.chinese: 优先购买  ； 抢先占有

examples.sentence: The company's preemption of the market prevented competitors from gaining a foothold.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + empt(拿/买) + ion(名词后缀) → 预先拿走 → 抢先占有

definitions.english: if a bird preens or preens itself, it cleans itself and makes its feathers smooth using its beak

examples.sentence: 50% of men under 35 spend at least 20 minutes preening themselves every morning in the bathroom.

mnemonics: 和green(n. 绿色)一起记

definitions.english: built from parts which are made in standard sizes so that they can be put together anywhere

examples.sentence: a prefabricated house

mnemonics: 来自prefabricate(v. 预制)

definitions.english: n a short introductory essay preceding the text of a book

examples.sentence: The author wrote a brief preface to explain the purpose of the research.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + face(脸/面) → 放在书最前面的脸面 → 序言

definitions.english: s serving as an introduction or preface

examples.sentence: He made a few prefatory remarks before beginning the main presentation.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + fat(说) + ory(形容词后缀) → 在前面说的话 → 前言的

definitions.english: like better; value more highly

examples.sentence: I prefer tea to coffee in the morning.

mnemonics: pre(在前) + fer(拿/带) → 拿到前面来 → 更喜欢

definitions.english: more desirable than another

examples.sentence: A quiet room is preferable to a noisy one for studying.

mnemonics: prefer(更喜欢) + able(能……的) → 能被更喜欢的 → 更可取的

definitions.english: more readily or willingly
definitions.chinese: 更可取地， 更好地， 宁可

examples.sentence: The report should be submitted by Friday, preferably before noon.

mnemonics: 来自prefer(v. 宁可， 更喜欢)

definitions.english: a strong liking

examples.sentence: I have a strong preference for coffee over tea in the morning.

mnemonics: pre(预先) + fer(拿/带) + ence(名词后缀) → 预先拿出来的 → 偏爱

definitions.english: s manifesting partiality

examples.sentence: The company offers preferential rates to long-term clients.

mnemonics: prefer(更喜欢) + ential(形容词后缀) → 更被喜欢的 → 优先的

definitions.english: to be a sign that something will happen later

examples.sentence: The wall through Berlin was finally ruptured, prefiguring the reunification of Germany.

mnemonics: pre(提前) + figure(形象) → 提前想好形象 → 预想

definitions.english: if a woman or female animal is pregnant, she has an unborn baby growing inside her body

examples.sentence: care for pregnant women
I knew right away that I was pregnant.
I thought I was too old to get pregnant .
I didn’t mean to get her pregnant (= make her pregnant ) .
His wife was heavily pregnant (= almost ready to give birth ) .

mnemonics: pre(在前面) + gn(出生) + ant → 尚未出生的 → 怀孕的

definitions.english: a prehensile tail, foot etc can curl around things and hold on to them

definitions.chinese: 恐外的， 恐惧外国人的

examples.sentence: Service in the armed forces gave many Americans a less xenophobic view of the world.

mnemonics: xeno(外来者) + phob(恐惧) + ic(形容词后缀) → 对外来者恐惧的

definitions.english: n plant adapted for life with a limited supply of water; compare hydrophyte and mesophyte

examples.sentence: The cactus is a classic xerophyte, storing water in its thick, fleshy stems to survive long droughts.

mnemonics: xero(干旱) + phyte(植物) → 旱生植物

definitions.english: a large boat with a sail, used for pleasure or sport, especially one that has a place where you can sleep

examples.sentence: His 36 ft yacht sank suddenly last summer.

mnemonics: 源自荷兰语jacht(狩猎/追逐) → 原指用于追逐海盗的快船，后演变为游艇

definitions.english: to suddenly pull something quickly and with force

examples.sentence: She yanked open the drawer.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模仿拉动时发出的声音，或联想yankee(美国佬)做事干脆利落，喜欢猛拉。

definitions.english: tell or spin a yarn

examples.sentence: She bought a ball of soft wool yarn to knit a sweater.
The old sailor loved to spin a yarn about his adventures at sea.

mnemonics: yarn(纱线) → 引申为纺织时拉出的长线 → 像讲故事一样把情节‘拉长’、‘编织’出来 → 奇谈

definitions.english: an erratic deflection from an intended course

examples.sentence: The pilot struggled to control the plane as it began to yaw in the strong crosswinds.

mnemonics: 联想记忆：发音类似“摇”，船或飞机在行驶中左右“摇”晃导致偏离航向。

definitions.english: an involuntary intake of breath through a wide open mouth; usually triggered by fatigue or boredom

examples.sentence: He tried to stifle a yawn during the long, monotonous lecture.
A deep canyon yawned before us, blocking our path.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模仿张大嘴巴发出‘呀’(ya)的声音 → 打呵欠

definitions.english: a racehorse considered one year old until the second Jan. 1 following its birth

examples.sentence: The yearling was put out to pasture to continue its development before training.

mnemonics: year(年) + ling(小后缀) → 一岁大的小动物

definitions.english: to have a strong desire for something, especially something that is difficult or impossible to get

examples.sentence: He yearned for freedom.

mnemonics: year(年) + n → 一年到头盼望 → 盼望， 渴望

definitions.english: a commercial leavening agent containing yeast cells; used to raise the dough in making bread and for fermenting beer or whiskey

examples.sentence: The baker added a pinch of yeast to the flour to help the bread rise.

mnemonics: yeast(谐音：一试) → 面团发酵效果好不好，一试便知。

definitions.english: bark in a high-pitched tone

examples.sentence: The puppy gave a sharp yelp when I accidentally stepped on its paw.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模仿狗受惊或疼痛时发出的尖锐叫声。

definitions.english: the basic unit of money in Japan; equal to 100 sen

examples.sentence: She has a yen to travel the world and experience different cultures.

mnemonics: yen(日元) → 早期日本贸易中对钱财的渴望 → 衍生为强烈的渴望

definitions.english: officer in the (ceremonial) bodyguard of the British monarch

examples.sentence: He lived the simple, independent life of a yeoman farmer.

mnemonics: yeo(古英语gēa，地区) + man(人) → 拥有土地的地区人 → 自耕农

definitions.english: an amount of a product

examples.sentence: The company's new investment is expected to yield high returns.
He refused to yield to the pressure of his colleagues.

mnemonics: 源自古英语gieldan(支付/偿还) → 支付出的产出 → 产量/产生

definitions.english: a surface that is yielding is soft and will move or bend when you press it

examples.sentence: the yielding softness of the bed

mnemonics: yield(屈服/出产) + -ing → 正在屈服的 → 顺从的/易弯曲的

definitions.english: a sharp high-pitched cry (especially by a dog)

examples.sentence: The small puppy gave a sharp yip when its tail was accidentally stepped on.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模仿小狗尖锐叫声的声音

definitions.english: a custard-like food made from curdled milk

examples.sentence: I like to add fresh berries and honey to my morning yogurt.

mnemonics: 源自土耳其语 yoğurt，意为浓稠的乳制品

definitions.english: fabric comprising a fitted part at the top of a garment

examples.sentence: The oxen were yoked together to plow the field.
They finally threw off the yoke of colonial rule.

mnemonics: yoke(形似牛轭) → 轭，连接

definitions.english: a person who is not very intelligent or interested in culture

examples.sentence: The city slickers laughed at the poor yokel who had never seen a subway before.

mnemonics: yoke(牛轭) + el(小人) → 戴着牛轭干活的人 → 乡下人

definitions.english: nutritive material of an ovum stored for the nutrition of an embryo (especially the yellow mass of a bird or reptile egg)

examples.sentence: The recipe calls for separating the egg white from the yolk.

mnemonics: yolk(蛋黄) 与 yellow(黄色) 词源相关，联想：蛋黄是黄色的

definitions.english: time long past

examples.sentence: Tales of yore tell of knights and dragons roaming the land.

mnemonics: yore(谐音：哟，儿) → 哟，儿时的记忆 → 往昔

definitions.english: if an animal or a person yowls, they make a long loud cry, especially because they are unhappy or in pain

examples.sentence: A tomcat was yowling out on the lawn.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模仿猫或动物发出长而尖锐的叫声（y-owl，像猫头鹰owl一样的叫声）

definitions.english: s extremely pleasing to the sense of taste

examples.sentence: Yes, thanks. It's yummy!
It was yummy.
I allow myself to eat one yummy dessert a week.

mnemonics: yum(象声词，形容吃东西的声音) + y(形容词后缀) → 美味的

definitions.english: a buffoon in one of the old comedies; imitates others for ludicrous effect

examples.sentence: The comedian is known for his zany sense of humor and unpredictable stage antics.

mnemonics: zan(音似：赞，指小丑表演让人点赞) + y(形容词后缀) → 滑稽的

definitions.english: excessive fervor to do something or accomplish some end

examples.sentence: He approached his new job with great zeal, working late into the night every day.

mnemonics: zeal(音似：智儿) → 聪明的孩子对学习充满热忱 → 热心

definitions.english: someone who has extremely strong beliefs, especially religious or political beliefs, and is too eager to make other people share them

examples.sentence: religious zealots

mnemonics: zeal(热情) + ot(人) → 充满热情的人 → 狂热者

definitions.english: extreme or excessive zeal or devotion

examples.sentence: Even so, there is some fear of zealotry.
But at a time when the western world is battling to defend free speech against religious zealotry, they look particularly indefensible.
Tory distrust of Europe has injected zealotry into what was once a pro-business party famed for its pragmatism.

mnemonics: zeal(热心) + otry(名词后缀，表示行为) → 过度的热心 → 狂热

definitions.english: s marked by active interest and enthusiasm

examples.sentence: The zealous volunteers worked through the night to complete the charity project.

mnemonics: zeal(热情) + ous(形容词后缀) → 充满热情的

definitions.english: the spirit of the time; the spirit characteristic of an age or generation
definitions.chinese: 时代精神， 时代思潮

examples.sentence: The novel perfectly captures the zeitgeist of the 1960s, reflecting the era's social unrest and idealism.

mnemonics: zeit(时间) + geist(精神) → 时代精神

definitions.english: the most successful point in the development of something

examples.sentence: Obama will be the zenith of black America for as long as he lives.
At the zenith of his artistic career, Elvis was outselling any other artist on the charts.

mnemonics: 源自阿拉伯语 samt (方向) → 演变为天顶概念 → 引申为顶峰

definitions.english: a soft gentle wind

examples.sentence: There was silence now except for the distant sea, a slight zephyr stirring the trees.

mnemonics: 来自希腊神话中的西风之神Zephyros

definitions.english: a mathematical element that when added to another number yields the same number

examples.sentence: The company's profit dropped to zero after the market crash.
He spent the morning zeroing his rifle for the competition.

mnemonics: 源自阿拉伯语 sifr (空)，象征圆圈(0)代表空无一物

definitions.english: eager interest and enjoyment
definitions.chinese: 刺激性； 兴趣， 热心

examples.sentence: The danger of being caught added a certain zest to the affair.

mnemonics: 对考试(test)有兴趣(zest)

definitions.english: s having an agreeably pungent taste
definitions.chinese: 兴致很高的， 热望的

examples.sentence: She added a zesty lemon dressing to the salad.
The team gave a zesty performance that energized the crowd.

mnemonics: 来自zest(n. 兴趣， 热心)

definitions.english: an angular shape characterized by sharp turns in alternating directions

examples.sentence: The path zigzagged down the hillside.

mnemonics: zig(锯齿状) + zag(锯齿状) → 像锯齿一样反复折转

definitions.english: a bluish-white lustrous metallic element; brittle at ordinary temperatures but malleable when heated; used in a wide variety of alloys and in galvanizing iron; it occurs naturally as zinc sulphide in zinc blende

examples.sentence: Galvanized steel is coated with a layer of zinc to prevent it from rusting.

mnemonics: 源自德语 Zink，因其结晶形状像锯齿(Zinke)而得名。

definitions.english: a large area that is different from other areas around it in some way

examples.sentence: San Francisco and Tokyo are both located in earthquake zones.
The government has set up a special economic zone to promote private enterprise.

mnemonics: zone(带子/地带) → 具有特定特征的带状区域

definitions.english: to increase suddenly and quickly

examples.sentence: Sales of the new electric car zoomed after the positive review.

mnemonics: 拟声词：模拟物体高速移动时发出的嗡嗡声 → 急速移动

examples.sentence: She performed the concerto with such éclat that the audience gave her a standing ovation.

mnemonics: 源自法语，词根écl- (爆发/闪耀) → 像光芒一样爆发出来的成就
